title: 第7章 风筝打法第8章 贪了一波
slug: 请不要给基础技能附魔奇怪的词条

灰语森林的夜，总是比黑石镇来得更早，也更深沉。
当维克多踏过那条无形的边界线——几棵被冒险者们用斧头砍出白色印记的老橡树——周围的世界仿佛瞬间切换了频道。
虫鸣声变得尖锐刺耳，空气中那股混合着腐殖质和松脂的味道陡然浓烈起来，温度也随着日落骤降。
他并没有深入森林腹地。
这是他第一次真正意义上的独自狩猎，维克多很清楚自己的斤两。哪怕背着黑角复合弓，在那些真正的掠食者面前，他依然只是一块口感不错的小点心。
他在森林边缘停了下来。这里是一处背风的小山坳，两块巨大的岩石夹角形成了一个天然的避难所。
维克多没有生火。在夜晚的森林里生火，等于向方圆五公里的魔兽发送“自助餐开业”的信号。
他从背包里掏出一包散发着刺激性气味的驱虫粉末，在岩石周围洒了一圈，然后开始布置警戒装置。
如果是老约翰，大概会在这里挖上两个捕兽夹，再设置几个精巧的套索。但维克多目前的技术还不足以搞出那么复杂的东西。他用的是最笨，但也最实用的办法。
几根坚韧的细鱼线，离地约二十厘米，横亘在几个必经的点位。线的另一端连接着悬挂在树干后的几串枯干的兽骨和坚硬的坚果壳。
“这就够了。”
维克多检查了一遍装置的灵敏度。在这个距离，任何试图靠近的大型生物都会绊动细线，发出清脆的响声。
对于现在的他来说，陷阱不需要杀伤敌人，只需要给他争取哪怕两秒钟的醒转时间，就足够决定生死了。
这一夜，维克多睡得很浅。他把那把精钢短剑抱在怀里，背靠着冰冷的岩石，每一次风吹过树梢的呜咽声，都能让他的眼皮微微颤动。
……
第二天清晨，阳光艰难地穿透茂密的树冠，在铺满枯叶的地面上投下斑驳的光影。
维克多嚼着干粮，就着冷水咽了下去。胃部的抽搐感提醒着他，身体需要热量。
他整理好装备，检查了弓弦的张力，将箭壶挂在最顺手的位置，然后猫着腰，像一只警惕的狸猫钻进了清晨的雾气中。
他的目标很明确：哥布林。

在黑石镇的冒险者协会，注册成为“见习冒险者”的门槛是提交五个哥布林的左耳。这不仅是一个身份认证，更是一张护身符。
这几天镇上的气氛越来越不对劲，那些贪婪的目光已经不仅仅是试探了。如果有了冒险者的身份，至少在明面上，受限于公会的庇护规则，那些人不敢做得太过分。
毕竟，每一个冒险者都是黑石镇贵重的资产，只有冒险者源源不断地从森林中带出战利品，才能支撑镇子上其他行业的繁荣。
维克多放轻脚步，顺着一条小道前行。
时不时的开启一会噪点伪装，从而清除一路上的痕迹。
约莫搜索了一个小时，在一片长满红色浆果的灌木丛附近，他发现了一串杂乱的脚印。
脚印很小，只有成人手掌的一半大，呈内八字，脚趾细长且深深陷入泥土。
“三个……不对，是三个半。”
维克多蹲下身，手指捻起一点泥土。脚印很新鲜，边缘的土还没干。其中一组脚印明显比其他的深，说明负重较大，或者体型更壮硕。
他顺着踪迹，小心翼翼地摸了过去。
几分钟后，顺风飘来了一股令人作呕的酸臭味——那是哥布林特有的体味，像是在下水道里发酵了三天的烂肉。
维克多屏住呼吸，伏在一处长满青苔的土坡后，慢慢探出了半个脑袋。
视野前方大约一百二十米的空地上，三只绿皮肤的小矮子正在争抢一只刚死不久的灰兔。
果然是标准的三人小队。
两只手持粗糙木棒和锈铁片打磨成的短刀，身材瘦小，正为了谁吃兔子头而互相撕咬耳朵。
而那个体型稍大的哥布林——大概有一米四左右，穿着一件破烂的皮甲，手里提着一根镶嵌着狼牙的骨棒，正一脚将另外两个同伴踹开，独霸了战利品。
“一只小头目，两只杂兵。”
维克多在心里迅速评估着战力对比。
距离一百二十米。风向……微弱的东南风，对自己有利。
“呼……”

维克多深吸一口气，调整着呼吸频率。他的瞳孔微微收缩，所有的杂念在这一刻被强制排除。
意念微动。
【噪点伪装，启动。】
嗡——
一种只有维克多自己能感觉到的低频嗡鸣声在大脑深处响起。视野边缘的景物开始出现轻微的扭曲，仿佛老式电视机的信号受到干扰。

Night in Gray Whisper Forest always comes earlier and deeper than in Blackstone Town.
When Victor stepped across the invisible boundary line—a few old oak trees that had been chopped with white marks by adventurers using axes—the world around him seemed to switch channels instantly.
The chirping of insects became sharp and harsh, the smell of humus and pine resin in the air suddenly became stronger, and the temperature also dropped sharply with the sunset.
He did not go deep into the heart of the forest.
This was his first real solo hunt, and Victor knew exactly what he was worth. Even with the black-horned compound bow on his back, he was still just a tasty snack in front of those real predators.
He stopped at the edge of the forest. Here is a small leeward col, and the angle between two huge rocks forms a natural shelter.
Victor didn't light a fire. Lighting a fire in the forest at night is equivalent to sending a "buffet is open" signal to the monsters within a five-kilometer radius.
He took out a packet of pungent-smelling insect repellent powder from his backpack, sprinkled it around the rocks, and then began to set up warning devices.
If it were Old John, he would probably dig two bear traps here and set up a few elaborate nooses. But Victor's current technology is not enough to create something that complicated. He used the stupidest but most practical method.
Several tough thin fishing lines, about 20 centimeters above the ground, lay across several must-pass points. The other end of the line is connected to several strings of dry animal bones and hard nut shells hanging behind the tree trunk.
"That's enough."
Victor checked the sensitivity of the device. At this distance, any large creature that tries to get close will trip on the thin line and make a crisp sound.
For him now, the trap does not need to kill the enemy. It only needs to buy him even two seconds to wake up, which is enough to decide life or death.
That night, Victor slept very lightly. He held the fine steel dagger in his arms and leaned against the cold rock. Every time the wind blew through the treetops, his eyelids trembled slightly.
…
Early the next morning, the sun struggled to penetrate the dense canopy of trees, casting mottled light and shadow on the ground covered with dead leaves.
Victor chewed the dry food and swallowed it with cold water. The twitching feeling in his stomach reminded him that his body needed heat.
He arranged the equipment, checked the tension of the bow string, hung the quiver in the most convenient position, and then ducked into the morning fog like a vigilant civet cat.
His target is clear: Goblins.
In the Adventurer Association of Blackstone Town, the threshold for registering as an "apprentice adventurer" is to submit the left ears of five goblins. This is not only an identity authentication, but also a talisman.
The atmosphere in the town has been getting worse and worse these days, and those greedy eyes are no longer just testing. If they have the status of adventurers, at least on the surface, they are limited by the guild's asylum rules, and those people dare not go too far.
After all, every adventurer is a valuable asset of Blackstone Town. Only adventurers who can continuously bring loot from the forest can support the prosperity of other industries in the town.
Victor walked lightly and followed a path.
Turn on noise camouflage from time to time to clear traces along the way.
After searching for about an hour, he found a series of messy footprints near a bush full of red berries.
The footprints are very small, only half the size of an adult's hand, and they are splayed. The toes are long and slender and sink deeply into the soil.
"Three...no, three and a half."
Victor knelt down and picked up a bit of soil with his fingers. The footprints were very fresh, and the soil at the edges was not yet dry. One set of footprints is obviously deeper than the others, indicating a heavier load or a stronger body.
He followed the trace and touched it carefully.
A few minutes later, a disgusting sour smell floated down the wind - it was the unique smell of goblins.The smell was like rotten meat that had been fermenting in the sewer for three days.
Victor held his breath, lay down behind a moss-covered slope, and slowly poked half of his head out.
In the open space about 120 meters in front of the field of vision, three green-skinned dwarfs were fighting for a gray rabbit that had just died.
It was indeed a standard three-person team.
The two were holding short knives made of rough wooden sticks and rusty iron pieces. They were thin and biting each other's ears over who would eat the rabbit's head.
And the slightly larger Goblin - about 1.4 meters tall, wearing a tattered leather armor, holding a bone club inlaid with wolf fangs in his hand, was kicking the other two companions away and monopolizing the spoils.
"One little boss, two miscellaneous soldiers."
Victor quickly assessed the comparison of combat power in his mind.
One hundred and twenty meters away. The wind direction...a weak southeasterly wind is favorable to me.
"Huh..."
Victor took a deep breath and adjusted his breathing rate. His pupils shrank slightly, and all distracting thoughts were forcibly eliminated at this moment.
Thoughts moved slightly.
[Noise camouflage, start. 】
Buzz——
A low-frequency buzzing sound that only Victor could feel sounded deep in his brain. The scenery at the edge of the field of vision began to appear slightly distorted, as if the signal of an old-fashioned television was being interfered with.
